subject: Term amendment: Dedicated capacity uptier + autoscale playbook
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme renewal – proposal prep

Vanessa / Tessa,

Quick sync before I send the formal amendment to Acme. They signaled they'll expand committed GPUs at renewal and want firm autoscale behavior in the contract. Key asks from discovery: +8 reserved A100s (steady), a warm pool for fast burst, and a throughput availability clause during high-traffic windows.

Questions for the proposal draft:
- Do we quote min/max replicas in the SOW or keep it operational (console-configured) with guaranteed throughput numbers?
- Warm pool — do we commit to a warm pool count and billing model (charged as reserved or as warm standby)?
- Scale-up lag SLA — can we offer a 60s target for cold-to-serving for warm pool misses, with fallbacks?

I started a skeleton SOW but want product/legal alignment first.

-Jordan

Attachments: redwood-draft-sow-notes.txt (notes)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>, Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity amendment proposal (Acme Analytics)

Hi Sara / Paul,

Thanks again for the call last week. As discussed, attached is a concise proposal for the upcoming contract adjustment so you can review with procurement:
- Acme-Dedicated-SOW-v2.pdf — summary of capacity, term, and commercial changes
- autoscale-playbook-acme.xlsx — proposed autoscale parameters and operational runbook
- redwood-term-amendment.docx — redlines for the existing Master Services Agreement (MSA) limited to capacity/ops items

Proposal highlights:
- Committed capacity: +8 A100 GPUs (reserved pool) added to your Dedicated cluster for the renewal term (12 months).
- Warm pool: 2 reserved warm nodes (billed at reduced standby rate). These are kept pre-initialized to reduce cold-starts for burst traffic.
- Autoscaling parameters (recommended and will be in playbook):
  * Min replicas (steady): 4 replicas
  * Max replicas (burst): 20 replicas (can be increased with 30d notice)
  * Warm pool count: 2 nodes (separate from min replica set)
  * Scale-up target: 45s for warm-pool transition, 120s for cold-start fallback
  * Grace windows: configurable per-route; default set to 60s evaluation
- Throughput guarantee: 95th percentile CPU/GPU availability aligned to a per-day token throughput floor (detailed in SOW).

Next steps: Please review the attachments and confirm which of the following you prefer (pick one):
A) Add numbers above as firm SOW commitments (we'll include explicit min/max replicas and warm pool counts in the SOW).
B) Keep the SOW capacity and commit to a throughput SLA only; autoscale knob values remain operational best-practice and editable by your platform team.

If you pick A, we'll include an amendment with explicit autoscale parameters and an escalation matrix for capacity events.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

Attachments: Acme-Dedicated-SOW-v2.pdf (pdf), autoscale-playbook-acme.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-term-amendment.docx (docx)
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity amendment proposal (Acme Analytics)

Vanessa — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side before we route to legal/procurement:

1) Billing model for warm pool: do we pay the full reserved rate or a reduced standby fee while nodes are warm but not serving steady traffic? Is that detailed in the SOW?
2) Scale-up target: 45s sounds reasonable; can you confirm that it includes model load (large model weights) and KV cache warm-up? We need an understanding of realistic tail latency for multi-tenant routing fallbacks.
3) Throughput guarantee: we need a weekday peak window guarantee (10:00–18:00 PT) with an option to buy additional burst tokens per-month rather than strict hard caps.

Also, Rachel from our infra team asked whether we can run a 2-week soak test at the beginning of the term to validate behavior under our production load before committing final numbers.

If you can provide a short one-page reply addressing the three bullets, procurement will be able to move the redline.

—Sara

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity amendment proposal (Acme Analytics)

Sara — thanks for the quick read. Answers below, and I've summarized the operational guarantee we can put in the SOW.

1) Warm-pool billing
- Proposal: Warm nodes are billed at a 60% reserved rate (i.e., 40% standby discount) when they are in warm standby but not carrying steady production traffic. If a warm node is actively serving user traffic it is billed at the reserved rate. This is captured in section 2.3 of the attached SOW (Acme-Dedicated-SOW-v2.pdf).

2) Scale-up target scope
- The 45s scale-up target covers instance bootstrap, model weight mapping for quantized models, and KV cache initialization for typical model sizes we discussed (up to 30B params quantized). For larger non-quantized weights we recommend the cold-start fallback of up to 120s.
- Note: this assumes your model variants remain within the performance profile in the model catalog. If you onboard bespoke larger models we will re-profile and may adjust temp targets.

3) Throughput guarantee and burst tokens
- We can commit to a weekday peak window availability SLA (10:00–18:00 PT) expressed as a token throughput floor (95th percentile not-to-exceed degradation). Pricing options: fixed floor in SOW OR a floor + prepaid burst token bucket (monthly). I've put both options in the appendix of the SOW for comparison.

4) Soak test
- We can do a 2-week soak test at term start; standard approach: we run it in production tenant with traffic mirroring and a pre-agreed test plan. Results will be inspected jointly; if we find systemic regressions we'll mutually agree remedial actions (no immediate billing changes unless agreed).

SOW language (draft) we can include if you choose Option A (firm autoscale parameters):
- "Redwood will provision a dedicated reserved pool of +8 A100-equivalent GPUs. Minimum serving replicas during steady state: 4. Maximum serving replicas for autoscale: 20. Warm pool: 2 nodes preserved for expedited scaling. Scale-up target from warm pool: 45 seconds; cold-start fallback target: 120 seconds. Redwood will use reasonable efforts to meet these targets and will provide runbook and post-incident reports if targets are not met."

If that looks good, I'll instruct legal to move the term amendment redline into DocuSign for signature. Which billing approach for warm pool do you prefer (reserved-rate billing vs discounted standby)?

Thanks — Vanessa

Attachments referenced: Acme-Dedicated-SOW-v2.pdf, autoscale-playbook-acme.xlsx
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2026 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme amendment — billing and soak test ops

Vanessa / team,

A couple internal notes if we go firm SOW:
- Operations: We should add a clause for a "soak test acceptance checklist" and an independent performance baseline report (signed by both parties) to protect us from post-signature rework requests. I'll draft the checklist and include the metrics we will capture (p95 token latency, scale-up time, memory usage, cache hit rate).
- Billing: Confirm that the 60% standby rate is applied pro-rata by hour, and that conversion from warm->active triggers full reserved billing immediately (we should log the timestamp for billing reconciliation).
- Escalations: Add an on-call contact list (we'll use the existing enterprise on-call rota) and a 4-step escalation path for capacity incidents.

I can fold these into redwood-term-amendment.docx before sending to legal.

—Rachel

Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity amendment proposal (Acme Analytics)

Vanessa / team — thanks for the clarifications. Procurement prefers Option A (firm SOW commitments) with the following small changes:
- Warm pool billing: we accept the 60% standby rate but request a monthly cap on combined standby charges (to avoid runaway costs during long warm periods).
- Soak test: 2-week soak test with acceptance checklist is acceptable; we request a joint sign-off step from our infra lead (Paul).
- Burst tokens: we will take the prepaid monthly burst bucket (please include pricing in the DocuSign package).

Assuming you include the monthly standby cap and the prepaid burst addendum, we are ready to route the amendment to our legal and signature. Please send the DocuSign when ready.

—Sara Patel
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Analytics
